newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrians seek referendums on sex equality, gene ban.
newsitem.headline: Austrians seek referendums on sex equality, gene ban.

text.p: Austrian pressure groups on Monday began gathering signatures for two separate petitions to try to force referendums on the issues of equality for women and banning genetically modified foods.

Women's groups are demanding equality be enshrined in the constitution and a series of measures be introduced such as a minimum wage, basic pension and preferential treatment in public tenders for firms that promote equality.
Environmentalists, fearing potential health risks, want a ban on the production and sale of genetically altered foods in Austria and on the use of genetically engineered plants.
Austria last week introduced a law stipulating that genetically modified foods must be labelled in an effort to bridge the gap until EU legislation, expected next month, comes into force.
Pressure groups Greenpeace Austria and Global 2000 argue that the law is not comprehensive enough.

Recent surveys have shown around 80 percent of Austrians do not want to see genetically engineered products on supermarket shelves, and two leading retailers Spar and Julius Meinl have instigated their own ban.

Support for the women's petition is harder to gauge, although both petitions are expected to bring in the necessary 100,000 signatures to force parliament to call a referendum. The petitioning will last until next Monday.
Such petitions are popular among activists and politicians in Austria as a means of applying pressure when the usual political channels are seen to be ineffective.
In recent years Austrians have petitioned on such issues as the retention of the country's neutrality, joining the EU and calling a halt to immigration.
